title: Ansel and the Wolf
premise: Xanthe Marchetti steals memories for coin in the valley of Hollowmere, the one place where magic cannot cross and where she has hidden since the covenant that sealed her people inside. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, she learns she carries a stolen memory that was never meant to leave the valley: the final recollection of the last dragon, whose dying flame sustains the covenant itself. Pursued by the wolf-warden Ansel—sworn to the realm she betrayed and bound to her by an old, half-forgotten love—she must carry the memory beyond the valley to reforge the covenant at the Ember Altar before the dragon-fire dies. Xanthe sacrifices her own treasured memories of Ansel to kindle the new flame, and though the covenant holds and the stars return, she must choose whether to trust love that begins again from nothing.
about_author: Gideon Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters never meant to be read, a habit that seeps into every story of memory and obligation. They live at the edge of a forest they refuse to name, writing fantasy that treats loyalty as both a wound and a gift.

chapters.title: The Thief of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the memory-market of Hollowmere, Xanthe lifts a grieving widow's worst night and sells it to a collector, establishing her trade and her rule: never steal anything that matters. Emotional beat: wry competence masking a fear that her own past has already been taken from her.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She breaks her rule for a client begging to forget a dead son, and the stolen memory burns strangely cold in her keeping. That night the stars above the valley go out one by one. Emotional beat: first crack in the safe, small life she has built.

chapters.title: The Warden at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The wolf-warden Ansel patrols the fallen border wards and finds wolf-sign where no wolf has walked in a generation, plus a thread of magic leading toward the city. Emotional beat: dread and recognition—he knows that thread, and he knows whose it is.

chapters.title: A Debt in Wolf's Clothing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel reaches Hollowmere under a truce banner and confronts Xanthe, who does not remember him though he clearly remembers her. He demands the stolen dragon-memory; she denies having it. Emotional beat: the ache of being a stranger to someone who once knew you completely.

chapters.title: The Ember Altar's Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe consults the blind archivist Odile, who reveals the valley's covenant: the last dragon gave its dying flame to seal magic out, and the wards' fall means the flame is guttering. The stolen memory in Xanthe's vault is the dragon's last recollection—the only seed that can regrow the fire. Emotional beat: horror at holding the world's lifeline without knowing it.

chapters.title: Everything She Stole
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe opens her private vault and finds the dragon-memory fused with a memory of her own—a night on the border with a young warden, a promise made in wolf-light. She realizes she sold pieces of her past to forget her crime: she stole from the dragon itself. Emotional beat: self-betrayal laid bare.

chapters.title: The Truce Breaks
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Hollowmere's council, learning what Xanthe carries, votes to destroy the memory rather than let magic return. Ansel is ordered to arrest her; instead he breaks her out of the wardhouse as the first creatures of the outer dark slip through the dead wards. Emotional beat: duty inverted—he betrays his post for the truth.

chapters.title: Running the Valley's Spine
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fugitives together, they flee north along the valley's ridge pursued by council hunters and things with too many joints. Ansel's wolf-shape carries them through a flooded gorge. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership hardening into trust, and the first flickers of her memory of him returning.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. They shelter in a village whose name the wards erased generations ago, where an old woman mistakes Ansel for her son. Xanthe sees what the covenant's price has done to ordinary lives. Emotional beat: guilt deepening—her people's safety was bought with everyone's forgetting.

chapters.title: What Ansel Gave Up
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Around the fire, Ansel tells her the truth: they were lovers before she crossed into the valley, and he let her go rather than drag her to the wardens. He has carried her memory for nine years. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; she remembers the promise but not the love.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Council hunter Sera Vance corners them with a proposal: surrender the memory to the council and Xanthe goes free—Sera's sister is trapped beyond the wards and the council's plan is to trade the dragon-memory to the outer powers for her return. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh; both plans demand sacrifice.

chapters.title: Creatures of the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The outer dark attacks at night; Ansel holds his wolf-form too long and begins losing himself to it. Xanthe pulls him back by speaking the words from their forgotten promise. Emotional beat: love as an anchor against dissolution—duty nearly devours him, memory saves him.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Odile catches up to them and confesses: she helped Xanthe steal from the dragon years ago, believing a broken covenant would free magic for the valley's oppressed. The wards' fall is partly her design. Emotional beat: the cost of righteous causes, and forgiveness neither easy nor complete.

chapters.title: The Border of Stars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the border where the wards fell and cross into the outer realm under a sky with no stars—only the guttering ember of the dragon-fire far off like a dying coal. Emotional beat: awe and terror at the world magic made; Xanthe feels her stolen memories stirring.

chapters.title: The Court of Ash
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Captured by the outer powers—ash-crowned lords who fed on the old covenant—they learn the truth: the lords engineered the wards' fall and want the dragon-memory to extinguish the flame forever. Emotional beat: the enemy's temptation—they offer Xanthe her complete past in exchange for the memory.

chapters.title: The Offer of a Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Imprisoned, Xanthe is shown her full stolen past, including the night of the theft and the love she erased. She can have it all back if she hands over the dragon-memory. Emotional beat: the central temptation—wholeness of self versus the lives of two realms.

chapters.title: Ansel's Choice
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel trades his warden's oath-cord—the source of his wolf-shape and his standing—to the ash court for Xanthe's freedom, becoming merely human and exile to both realms. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over duty, love over self, mirroring and exceeding her earlier sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Ember Altar
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They fight through the ash court to the Ember Altar as the last dragon-fire gutters. Sera arrives—not to stop them but to help, choosing truth over her sister, and holds the passage open. Emotional beat: allies converging, every debt called in at once.

chapters.title: What Xanthe Burns
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The altar demands memory as fuel. Xanthe feeds it the dragon-memory and then her own restored past—the love, the theft, the years—giving the flame everything she is to reforge the covenant. Emotional beat: climax and sacrifice; she wakes with no memory of Ansel at all, and the stars reignite.

chapters.title: The Covenant Remade
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The new covenant binds the realms not by forgetting but by honest exchange—magic and memory may cross freely, guarded by wardens who choose. Ansel, oathless, is offered wardenship anew; the ash court crumbles into ordinary stone. Emotional beat: hard-won resolution, a world remade on better terms.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Back in Hollowmere, Xanthe rebuilds her life, haunted by a warmth she cannot name. A man with a wolf's eyes appears at her market stall and asks, gently, to tell her a story. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope—love beginning again from nothing.

chapters.title: The First Memory of Us
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. As Ansel tells their story, fragments return to Xanthe—not restored, but newly made, theirs together. She chooses him not from memory but from the present tense, and the valley's first starlit festival begins. Emotional beat: resolution and renewal; love against duty resolved into love freely chosen, with the future open.
